title: Declare model runtime signatures and version-affinity endpoint
creator: Anika Shah
description: We need a new, stable API surface to publish machine-readable runtime signatures (performance and capability profiles) alongside model manifests and to expose version-affinity/pinning metadata used by smart routing and fallbacks. This ticket defines the schema, rollout constraints, and the API endpoints for querying and updating model runtime signatures and version affinity. The goal is to enable clients (Console, SDKs, routing layer) to make deterministic routing/selection and pinning decisions without calling internal heuristics. The schema must be compact, stable for at least one major release, and redact sensitive hardware-specific metrics while providing actionable fields for batching, caching, and cost estimation.
acceptance_criteria: Define a v1 runtime_signature schema that includes capability flags and performance bounds and document field semantics
Add /v1/models/:model_id/runtime-signature GET endpoint returning the runtime_signature and a list of published versions with per-version affinity metadata
Add /v1/models/:model_id/versions/:version/pin PATCH endpoint that updates pinning policy (strict/soft/fallback) and records time and actor
Backward-compatibility: existing /models/:id/manifest endpoints continue to work; new fields are optional and the service tolerates missing runtime_signature
Console shows per-model recommended batch size and max_context derived from runtime_signature within the catalog page (feature flag gated)
Unit and integration tests for schema validation, read/write authorization (RBAC), and graceful fallback when fields are missing
SDKs (js/py) have thin mapping helpers to interpret runtime_signature and pin policy (PRs merged)
design_decisions: Expose only aggregated performance signals (p50/p95 tokens/sec, recommended_batch, kv_cache_effective_mb) to avoid leaking exact hardware or kernel telemetry
Use explicit capability booleans (supports_streaming, supports_functions, supports_structured_outputs) instead of free-form capability strings to simplify client logic
Pinning policy modeled as enum {strict, soft, none} with an optional fallback list of pinned version ids and affinity scores in [0.0,1.0]
Keep schema names short (snake_case) to reduce payload size for high-cardinality model catalogs
Runtime_signature is versioned with a metadata field spec_version and deprecation hints (deprecation_date) to allow iterative schema evolution
All write operations require workspace-level permission model: model:write or catalog:maintain. Read requires model:read. Console feature will be behind 'catalog_profile_v1' feature flag initially
implementation_tasks: API: add GET /v1/models/:model_id/runtime-signature (controller + service layer + caching)
API: add PATCH /v1/models/:model_id/versions/:version/pin (authorization + audit log entry)

DB: add runtime_signatures table (model_id, spec_version, payload_json, published_by, published_at) and version_affinity table (model_id, version_id, affinity_score, pin_policy, updated_by, updated_at)
Migration: backfill lightweight runtime_signature for existing catalog entries using heuristic defaults and mark 'estimated: true'
SDK: add helpers in js/py to parse runtime_signature and enforce client-side sanity checks (max_context sanity clamp)
Console: catalog card display for recommended_batch, max_context, supports_streaming (behind feature flag)
Tests: schema contract tests, API auth tests, end-to-end routing simulation against runtime_signature-driven decision-making
Docs: OpenAPI update, migration guide for partners, and changelog entry
